column3: The Hebrew title names the house; BSB specifies the temple.
The Hebrew explicitly names my soul; BSB says me.
The Hebrew names the remembrance of His holiness; BSB says His holy name.
The Hebrew places a moment in His anger and life in His favor without explicit lasts verbs.
The Hebrew joins favor and establishing strength for the mountain in one clause; BSB separates favoring me from making the mountain strong.
The Hebrew uses uncompleted verbs of calling and pleading; BSB uses past verbs.
The Hebrew names blood without an explicit shedding; BSB says bloodshed.
The Hebrew’s command to hear leaves the object unstated; BSB supplies me.
The Hebrew says You loosened sackcloth and girded me with joy; BSB says peeled it off and clothed me.
The Hebrew names glory as the singing subject; BSB says my heart.
